## What's new

### Linux
- **Linux builds for the first time:** an AppImage (updates itself), plus `.deb` and `.rpm` packages. They are untested on a real Linux desktop, so please report problems.

### First run and reading
- **A short first-run setup** for theme, size, mode, script style, language and word meanings. Skip it any time.
- **Word meanings follow your translation's language**, not just English.
- **Verse by Verse is the default mode**, including for the verse of the day.
- **The bundled text and page fonts refresh weekly** in the background (online only), so corrections reach you without a new installer.

### Listening
- **92 more reciters that play whole surahs**, listed separately as Listen only, and bigger speed and volume icons in the player.

### Picks up where you left off
- **Continue where I left off** (on by default, in Settings): the app reopens on the surah and verse you were reading, in both Verse by Verse and Reading modes. Turn it off to always start at Al-Fatihah.
- The player bar now shows when you hover it, by default.

### Settings
- **Reorganised into 8 pages** (Appearance, Translation & meanings, Mushaf pages, Listening, Reminders, App & window, Data & help, About) with search across every setting.
- **Reset a single setting, see everything you changed from the default, or reset all.**
- **A new About page** with the version, updates, source code link, the website (qurandesktop.netlify.app) and developer details.

### Look and feel
- **A custom tooltip everywhere**, with the keyboard shortcut shown as a key. The zoom buttons show the percentage they change to.
- **Zoom, Fit and Fill** for the interface, and a new **Black and gold** theme.
- **A bigger first-run setup** whose theme and script previews match the ones in Settings, with a clearer marker for the current step.
- **Reciter portraits** for more reciters, bundled in the app so they show offline.

### Fixes
- **Reopening from the tray:** the top bar and player could be missing, with the page scrolled out of place. The app now re-measures the window and resets the scroll when it comes back.
- **Uninstaller:** it now shows the Quran icon instead of the default one.
